name: Forge Domain
label: Divine Domain
summary: A divine smith who crafts magic items overnight and wears armor blessed to turn blades.
flavor: The gods of the forge are patrons of artisans who work with metal — armorers, weaponsmiths, and jewelers. Their clerics see the act of creation as sacred, and the tempering of steel as a metaphor for the tempering of the soul.
playstyle: The tankiest cleric. Blessing of the Forge grants a permanent +1 item, Soul of the Forge adds +1 AC on top of heavy armor, and Saint of Forge and Fire gives fire immunity plus resistance to nonmagical weapons.

features.name: Bonus Proficiencies
features.description: You gain proficiency with heavy armor and smith's tools.

features.name: Blessing of the Forge
features.description: At the end of a long rest, you can touch one nonmagical object that is a suit of armor or a simple or martial weapon. Until your next long rest or your death, the object becomes a magic item granting a +1 bonus to AC (if armor) or a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls (if a weapon).

features.name: Channel Divinity: Artisan's Blessing
features.description: You conduct an hour-long ritual to create a simple metal item — a weapon, armor, ten pieces of ammunition, a set of tools, or similar — worth no more than 100 gp. You must have metal worth at least equal to the finished item's value, which the ritual consumes.

features.name: Soul of the Forge
features.description: You gain resistance to fire damage, and while wearing heavy armor you gain a +1 bonus to AC.

features.name: Divine Strike
features.description: Once on each of your turns when you hit with a weapon attack, you can cause the attack to deal an extra 1d8 fire damage. This increases to 2d8 at 14th level.

features.name: Saint of Forge and Fire
features.description: You gain immunity to fire damage, and while wearing heavy armor you have resistance to bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage from nonmagical attacks.
